Added the `params` MAP<STRING, STRING> column to the Parquet writer in the flusher for full Iceberg schema compatibility.

## Changes Made
- Added `MapArray` and `OffsetBuffer` imports for map type support
- Implemented columnar map array construction for the `params` field
- Added `params` field to Arrow schema with `DataType::Map`
- Included `params_array` in the RecordBatch output
- Added unit tests for params serialization (populated and empty maps)

## Retrospective
- **What worked:** The existing columnar Parquet writer infrastructure was well-designed; adding the params map was straightforward by following the same pattern as other fields.
- **What didn't:** N/A - implementation worked on first attempt.
- **Surprise:** The Arrow MapArray API requires building offsets manually and wrapping values in a StructArray - more verbose than simple array types.
- **Reusable pattern:** For adding map columns to Parquet in Arrow: build key/value vectors, compute offsets, create StructArray, wrap in MapArray with proper field definition.
issue.title: Flusher: Parquet writer with columnar schema

issue.description:
Plan: docs/plan/plan.md §Phase 2 L154-159 — "Deployment: Target ardenone-manager
cluster; Services: Collector + Flusher deployments; Persistent volume for shared logs".

## Observed (plan-vs-built sweep 2026-08-19)
All three pods have been Pending for 56 days and can never schedule:

    kubectl -n trace get pods
      trace-collector-776fc78684-2bbgl  0/1 Pending  56d
      trace-collector-776fc78684-wls2c  0/1 Pending  56d
      trace-flusher-6d6bc686dc-t7hfs    0/1 Pending  56d

    describe -> FailedScheduling (x4086 over 14d):
      "0/1 nodes are available: pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims"

    kubectl -n trace get pvc
      trace-dlq   Pending  nfs-client  56d
      trace-logs  Pending  nfs-client  56d

Root cause: both PVCs request storageClassName "nfs-client", which does not exist on
this cluster. The only classes available are:
      local-path (default)  rancher.io/local-path            WaitForFirstConsumer
      nfs-synology          ...synology-nfs...provisioner    Immediate

Set in declarative-config/k8s/ardenone-manager/trace/pvc.yaml:14 (50Gi) and
dlq-pvc.yaml:14 (5Gi).

The fix is a declarative-config commit -> ArgoCD sync. Do NOT kubectl patch the PVCs;
a PVC's storageClassName is immutable anyway, so the existing two must be deleted and
recreated by ArgoCD after the manifest change -- confirm nothing on them is worth
keeping first (they never bound, so they hold no data).

Choose nfs-synology (Immediate binding, ReadWriteMany-capable, matches the "shared
logs" intent) unless a reason to prefer local-path is recorded in the commit message.

## Done when
    kubectl --server=http://traefik-ardenone-manager:8001 get pvc -n trace
-> both trace-dlq and trace-logs show STATUS Bound

    kubectl --server=http://traefik-ardenone-manager:8001 get pods -n trace
-> trace-collector and trace-flusher pods are Running, 1/1 Ready
issue.notes:
OUTCOME: The prescribed storage-class fix is already implemented, synced and verified live. No file changes were needed - the Done-when 'pods Running' half is blocked by a DIFFERENT, unrelated defect, so I am not closing this bead.

declarative-config commit 559649b9 already renamed both PVCs and pointed them
at a class that exists:

  k8s/ardenone-manager/trace/dlq-pvc.yaml -> trace-dlq-v2,  5Gi, nfs-synology
ArgoCD app trace-ns-ardenone-manager applied them; both are Bound:
  trace-logs-v2  Bound  nfs-synology  50Gi  RWX
  trace-dlq-v2   Bound  nfs-synology   5Gi  RWX
That is exactly the change this bead asked for, including the nfs-synology
choice (Immediate binding, RWX, matches shared-logs intent). Both Deployments
in git already reference the -v2 claims. The trace path in declarative-config
is clean - no uncommitted work.

WHY THE PODS ARE STILL NOT RUNNING (not a storage problem):
Both Deployments pull ghcr.io/jedarden/trace-{collector,flusher}:latest and
that image was NEVER PUBLISHED. Zero trace workflows have ever run in iad-ci -
the trace-collector-ci / trace-flusher-ci templates exist but were never

Forbidden' from ghcr.io, matching an external registry probe. So:
  trace-collector-657df696b9-6gtfh  ImagePullBackOff
  trace-flusher-659986977c-g289v    ImagePullBackOff
The revision-1 pods this bead originally described are still Pending only
because the rollout never completed and Kubernetes retains old replicas
until the new ones go Ready.

Follow-up filed as trace-2bff0f00 (publish the images + fix the prohibited
:latest tag + resolve registry auth). That bead is the actual blocker for
this bead's 'pods Running 1/1 Ready' criterion.

The old trace-logs / trace-dlq PVCs still exist because the ArgoCD app uses
PruneLast=true and every sync fails on the Deployment progress deadline, so

Verified live 2026-09-06 on ardenone-manager (namespace trace).

Both trace Deployments reference ghcr.io/jedarden/trace-collector:latest and
ghcr.io/jedarden/trace-flusher:latest. Those images were never published - the
trace-collector-ci / trace-flusher-ci WorkflowTemplates exist in
declarative-config (k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows) but ZERO trace workflows have
ever run in iad-ci, so kaniko has never pushed them.

Symptom (NOT a storage problem - the PVCs are Bound):
  trace-collector-657df696b9-6gtfh  0/1  ImagePullBackOff
  trace-flusher-659986977c-g289v    0/1  ImagePullBackOff
Pod message: 'failed to fetch anonymous token: unexpected status from GET
request to https://ghcr.io/token?... 403 Forbidden' - i.e. the package does
not exist / is not public.

Two decisions this bead must make before it can be closed:
1. Registry + auth. Every working ghcr.io image on ardenone-manager is a
   third-party PUBLIC image. There is no precedent for pulling first-party
   images from ghcr.io/jedarden anonymously, and namespace trace has no
   imagePullSecrets (the only pull secret in the cluster is
   docker-hub-registry, used elsewhere). Either publish the ghcr packages
   public, add an imagePullSecret, or move to ronaldraygun/* on Docker Hub
   like the rest of the fleet - and update the CI templates to match.
2. Tag policy. Both Deployments currently use :latest, which is prohibited.
   Whatever image this bead publishes, the Deployments must be pinned to a
   semver tag in declarative-config/k8s/ardenone-manager/trace/. Note the CI
   templates only push :latest for a stable vX.Y.Z tag, so passing a semver
   tag yields both.

Also note: the rollout is stuck (revision 2 never became Ready), so the old
revision-1 ReplicaSets still hold their Pending pods and still reference the
removed trace-logs/trace-dlq PVCs. Those PVCs survive only because the
ArgoCD app sets PruneLast=true and the sync keeps failing on the Deployment
progress deadline - once this bead makes the pods healthy, the next
successful sync prunes them automatically. Do not kubectl delete them.

Storage-class work itself is DONE and verified - see trace-29c20038.

issue.notes:
AUDIT RESULT (2026-09-07, iad-ci / argo-workflows, credential-free + ro-kubeconfig reads; no credential value printed at any point):

1) ghcr-credentials: PRESENT, keys match.
- type kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson, single key .dockerconfigjson; auths contain exactly ghcr.io, login jedarden.
- Referenced identically by BOTH trace-collector-ci and trace-flusher-ci: spec.volumes[] name=ghcr-config -> secretName=ghcr-credentials, items .dockerconfigjson -> config.json, volumeMounted at /kaniko/.docker in the docker-build-push step (kaniko default auth path). No mismatch.
- Validity by result: ghcr.io /token exchange for repository:jedarden/trace-collector:pull,push -> 200 with token issued; bearer proven usable by tags/list 200 on existing packages (jedarden/seam = 5 tags, jedarden/vista = 7 tags). Push scope approved at exchange on both trace targets; an actual push cannot be verified read-only.

2) github-token (GH_TOKEN): PRESENT, referenced correctly.
- Opaque, single key 'token'; both templates set env GH_TOKEN via secretKeyRef {name: github-token, key: token} in the git-checkout step. No mismatch.
- Validity by result: GET api.github.com/user with the token -> 200 as user jedarden (type User), scopes: repo, workflow, write:packages. Also accepted as a ghcr.io registry credential (token exchange 200).

3) Expected non-findings: ghcr.io/jedarden/trace-collector and trace-flusher packages do not exist yet (tags/list 404 NAME_UNKNOWN) and zero trace-* workflows have ever run in argo-workflows - consistent with a pre-first-run state, not an auth problem.

4) Hygiene: the SAME classic PAT is shared across three secrets (ghcr-credentials, github-token, ghcr-jedarden-registry) and carries broad scopes repo+workflow+write:packages, far more than registry work needs. Recommend splitting into narrowly-scoped tokens. forgejo-container-registry is a distinct credential (correct). GH_TOKEN is currently declared but never consumed in either template - the clone uses the Forgejo credential helper and kaniko uses only the mounted config.json.

5) INCIDENT DISCLOSURE: during verification, an over-broad jq ('..|strings') extraction printed the ghcr.io token-exchange response's token field - which echoes base64(PAT) - into this session's transcript, so the PAT is recoverable from it. Rotation of that PAT plus an update to all three secrets above is recommended as a follow-up. No credential value was written to this bead, to git, or to any file.

Completed core analytics query library for three primary metrics.

Created three DuckDB query files in analytics/queries/:

1. **core_ctr.sql** (4414 bytes) - CTR by campaign/ad/creative
   - CTR by campaign with network breakdown
   - CTR by creative (headline + image combinations)
   - Daily CTR trends by network
   - Campaign x Creative matrix for fatigue analysis

2. **core_dwell_time.sql** (7940 bytes) - Aggregate heartbeat pings into time-on-page
   - Dwell time by session using explicit dwell events
   - Dwell time by landing page (aggregated)
   - Dwell time by campaign/creative for performance correlation
   - Inferred dwell time from event sequences (for sessions without explicit dwell events)
   - Dwell time distribution histogram

3. **core_funnel.sql** (12281 bytes) - Session chain from ad click to conversion
   - Full funnel analysis by campaign (impression → click → engagement → conversion)
   - Funnel by creative (headline + image performance)
   - Drop-off analysis identifying where users abandon
   - Time-to-convert analysis
   - Daily funnel trend monitoring

All queries use the standard template format ({{events_table}}, {{start_date}}, {{end_date}}) and are compatible with both Iceberg and Parquet views.

## Retrospective
- **What worked:** Leveraged existing schema files (sessions_iceberg.sql, ad_events_iceberg.sql) to understand the data model before writing queries. The template format used by existing queries (campaign_funnel.sql, ctr_by_campaign.sql) provided a consistent pattern.
- **What didn't:** Initially considered using raw event sequences for dwell time, but realized the schema includes explicit dwell_time_ms and dwell_visible_pct fields from V003 migration, making queries more accurate.
- **Surprise:** The schema already has comprehensive engagement metrics (scroll_depth_pct, scroll_time_ms, dwell_time_ms, dwell_visible_pct) added in V003, reducing the need for complex inference logic.
- **Reusable pattern:** Core analytics queries should be organized by metric type (CTR, dwell time, funnel) with multiple variants per file (by dimension, aggregated, trends) for comprehensive coverage.

- **What worked:** Leveraged existing normalization.sql patterns for consistent cross-network schema
- **What didn't:** Initially considered just updating generic events table, but ad analytics need dedicated normalized fields
- **Surprise:** Existing docs already had Trino syntax for MAP types
- **Reusable pattern:** For adding new fields: collector -> validator -> flusher -> Iceberg schema -> docs

Removed the prohibited CronJob manifests, preserved the analytics UI in analytics-ui.yaml, and moved analytics/compaction scheduling onto Deployments with internal loops; validated k8s kinds and pushed commit 6b0550e.

Added the analytics, compactor, and syncer CI WorkflowTemplates under declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/, committed and pushed them, and verified all three live in argo-workflows with ArgoCD resource status Synced.
